candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

Dear Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with the Adolescent Wellness Academy as you expand into North Carolina. With more than 20 years of experience in adolescent behavioral health, residential and PHP/IOP leadership, clinical operations, and program development, I have built a career dedicated to helping teens and families navigate high stress moments with clarity, compassion, and evidence based support. As a licensed Marriage and Family Therapist, the mission and values of AWA align deeply with my own leadership philosophy and the environments I strive to create.
My entrepreneurial background includes creating, launching and scaling inpatient and outpatient programs, overseeing multidisciplinary clinical and operational teams, and building high quality workflows that support strong outcomes and regulatory compliance. I have led admissions processes, treatment planning, crisis response, and discharge coordination while ensuring documentation quality, accreditation readiness, and risk management. 
I am particularly energized by the opportunity to lead AWA’s first North Carolina facility. I have a proven track record of building values driven cultures where staff feel supported, challenged, and connected to a shared mission. My leadership style is collaborative and people first, clear, and accountable, rooted in radical candor, consistent feedback, and a commitment to helping teams grow. I am skilled at developing talent, managing performance, and fostering environments where clinicians and staff can deliver exceptional care.
I would love the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s expansion, and create a premier resource for adolescents and their families seeking behavioral health services. Thank you for your consideration, and I look forward to the possibility of contributing to AWA’s mission and supporting the successful launch of your North Carolina clinic.
Sincerely,
Dr. Sarah Stuchell, PhD, LMFT

Statesville, North Carolina

October 14, 2026


Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

Ana Valle-Peters

I am writing to express my interest in opportunities where I can use my operations and administrative
experience while continuing to make a positive difference for students, families, and the people who
support them. I bring more than nine years of experience working in a nonprofit public charter school,
where I have supported both the day-to-day operations of the organization and the needs of its school
community.

Stacy Zenteno

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Behavioral Health position. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, program development, and organizational leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise and operational management experience that aligns well with the demands of overseeing behavioral health programs serving adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in program operations, staff supervision, quality improvement, regulatory compliance, and multidisciplinary collaboration. As the founder and Clinical Director of a behavioral health practice, I have directed clinical and administrative operations, developed policies and procedures, managed budgets and performance oversight, and led a multidisciplinary team of seven therapists and two administrative staff. My responsibilities have required balancing clinical quality, operational efficiency, ethical standards, and organizational growth while maintaining a strong commitment to individualized, trauma-informed care.

My experience also includes direct work with youth and vulnerable populations. As a Program Coordinator with Teen Living Programs, I supported children, youth, and young adults experiencing housing instability, coordinated community partnerships, supervised staff and interns, and contributed to program development and resource allocation. Thank you for your consideration.


All the best,

Stefany Gamba

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Hiring Committee

Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Subject: Employment Opportunity at Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in an employment opportunity with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over six years of experience in behavioral health, mental health support, and working with children, adolescents, and adults facing emotional and behavioral challenges, I believe my background and dedication would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have gained valuable experience in residential treatment facilities, educational settings, and direct support roles. These opportunities have strengthened my skills in crisis intervention, behavioral management, conflict resolution, de-escalation, and providing compassionate, individualized care. I understand the importance of creating a safe, structured, and supportive environment where adolescents feel respected, understood, and encouraged to succeed.

I am currently pursuing my Bachelor’s degree in Behavioral Health Science at Grand Canyon University to further expand my knowledge and professional development. My goal is to continue making a positive impact in the mental health field by supporting individuals through difficult situations and helping them develop healthier coping skills.

I would bring patience, reliability, strong communication skills, and a genuine passion for helping young people overcome challenges. I believe every adolescent deserves guidance, encouragement, and someone who recognizes their potential.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and dedication align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team.

Sincerely,
Donica Hunt Jr.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in behavioral health, human services, crisis intervention, and customer service, I am passionate about helping individuals and families navigate challenging situations and connect with the support they need. I would welcome the opportunity to use my communication skills, compassion, and attention to detail to help clients take the first step toward recovery and wellness.

In my previous roles as a Behavioral Health Technician at Gibault Children's Services and a Mental Health Technician at Harsha Behavioral Center, I provided direct support to individuals with behavioral and mental health needs, including children with autism and behavioral challenges. These experiences strengthened my ability to remain calm in difficult situations, listen attentively, respond appropriately to sensitive concerns, and communicate with individuals who may be experiencing emotional distress. I understand the importance of treating every individual with dignity, patience, and compassion, especially when they and their families are seeking help during vulnerable moments.

My experience as a Customer Care Representative with Continuum Global Solutions also prepared me to succeed in a client-facing admissions role. I handled incoming calls from healthcare professionals, answered questions, explained insurance policy information, and worked to resolve concerns efficiently. Combined with my behavioral health experience, this background has equipped me to communicate clearly, provide supportive service, and help people understand their options. I also bring experience with clinical documentation, HIPAA compliance, confidential information, and accurate recordkeeping, all of which are essential when managing admissions inquiries and coordinating care.

Additionally, my current experience in quality assurance has strengthened my ability to follow established procedures, review records for accuracy, identify discrepancies, and maintain compliance with organizational standards. I am organized, adaptable, dependable, and comfortable prioritizing responsibilities in fast-paced environments. I would bring these strengths to managing inquiries, documenting interactions, following up with prospective clients and families, and helping ensure a smooth transition from the initial call to the next step in the admissions process.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines my experience in behavioral health with my commitment to helping people access meaningful care. I would be proud to contribute to a team that recognizes the importance of making every caller feel heard, respected, and supported. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to compassionate service could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Kandyse Lewis

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Master of Social Work, a bachelor's degree in Psychology, and more than ten years of experience in education and peer counseling, I bring a strong foundation in human behavior, communication, assessment, and supporting individuals and families through challenging situations.

In my current role as a Peer Counseling Teacher, I work with adolescents to address interpersonal challenges, develop coping and communication skills, resolve conflicts, and navigate sensitive personal and social concerns. My work requires patience, active listening, sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to build trust while communicating clearly with students, families, and colleagues. I also develop support programs, coordinate resources, and collaborate with others to address individual needs and promote student well-being.

My education in social work and psychology has strengthened my understanding of behavioral health, adolescent development, family dynamics, and the importance of connecting people with appropriate support. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming experience for individuals and families. I would approach each interaction with compassion, professionalism, and respect, helping callers understand their options and the next steps in the process.

I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents and families seeking mental health services through Adolescent Wellness Academy. I would welcome the opportunity to apply my counseling-related skills, organizational abilities, and commitment to helping others in a role focused on making the treatment access process more supportive and manageable.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my educational background, professional experience, and commitment to compassionate service could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Renee Golembiowski, MSW

Colorado Springs, CO 80925 ♦ brianna.l.gabbard@gmail.com 

October 22, 2026

RE: Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager: I am writing to express my interest in the position of Virtual Admissions Coordinator for Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment. I am currently pursuing a Master of Arts in Counseling and Human Services with a concentration in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and I am eager to build upon my professional experience while developing my skills as a counselor in a clinical setting.

For nearly a decade, I have worked in secondary education with students and families from a wide range of backgrounds and circumstances. Throughout my career, I have had the opportunity to work alongside individuals from low-socioeconomic and historically disenfranchised populations, as well as individuals whose lives have been impacted by addiction, legal involvement, housing instability, and homelessness. These experiences have shaped the way I understand people and the circumstances that influence their lives. More importantly, they have reinforced my belief that every person deserves to be heard, treated with dignity, and supported without judgment.

My experience in education has taught me that meaningful change often begins with a trusting relationship. As an educator, I have learned to listen carefully, recognize when someone may be struggling beneath the surface, meet individuals where they are, and provide support while respecting their autonomy. I have also seen how trauma, substance use, socioeconomic barriers, family circumstances, and other challenges can affect a person's ability to succeed. These experiences have been an important part of my decision to pursue clinical mental health counseling and licensed addiction counseling.

As a graduate student, I am now seeking an opportunity to translate my academic preparation into meaningful clinical experience. I am most interested in strengthening my counseling skills alongside qualified professionals, developing greater confidence in clinical assessment and treatment, and becoming more intentional in how I support clients through difficult periods of their lives. At this present stage, curiosity, genuineness, and adaptability are the core values that drive my professional attitude. 
I would be grateful for the opportunity to learn and serve at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to have the opportunity to grow within your organization while gaining the clinical experience necessary to become a compassionate, ethical, and effective practitioner.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my background, goals, and interest in potentially working with the Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Brianna L. Gabbard

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. My name is Gabriela Lloyd-Perez, and I am thrilled at the opportunity to join your team and support your mission of promoting mental health and emotional well-being for adolescents.

What I find most appealing about this particular position is the opportunity to work closely with families who want to support their teens' mental health. As someone who has personally struggled with mental health as a teenager, I understand the importance of having a strong support system and being able to connect with experienced professionals who can guide and consult. I am deeply passionate about using my own experiences to help others, and I believe that this role would allow me to do just that.

Having worked for several years already with Vibrant Emotional Health in the Disaster Distress Helpline’s Online Peer Support Program (DDH OPSC), I worked specifically with parents and caregivers to provide resources to assist with their children and teens. While employed in this role,  I was promoted to the position of protocol and documentation; through this, I developed strong skills in program coordination. I have worked with several individuals in management to see through the creation to implementation of several crucial documents for the program. 

 In addition, I trained crisis counselors on the 988 crisis line and for the LGBTQI youth chat and text line. During my time in this position, I was able to assess callers who reached out to the 988 line for suicidal ideation and imminent danger. I was able to provide resources and schedule follow-up calls. 

Furthermore, I am highly organized, detail-oriented, and have excellent time management skills. I understand the importance of meeting deadlines and ensuring that programs run smoothly. I am also proficient in Microsoft Office and have experience working with databases and managing program budgets. I have also worked remotely for over 5 years and understand the skills needed to work independently. 

Aside from my technical skills, I am a strong advocate for mental health. I am also a certified Mental Health First Aid responder and have completed several trainings on suicide prevention. I am always looking for opportunities to expand my knowledge and skills in the mental health field, and I am excited about the prospect of continuing this in this position. 

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss my qualifications further.

Sincerely,

Gabriela Lloyd-Perez

At the end of the home visit, Investigator and family work together to form a Treatment Plan with immediate goals to minimize imminent dangers, while investigator makes referrals for the next stage of treatment for the family, which include referrals to community resources as deemed necessary. Very detailed documentation is extremely necessary in every case. Contact all professionals who have observed the family and inquire about any concerns for the children or the family. These professionals may include, but are not limited to: Teachers, School Admin, Counselors, Doctors, Nurses, other family and friends, who reside outside of the home. Cases are only completed when imminent dangers are controlled/minimized and there are no concerns about reported or new risks and/or harm, as the family is referred to services. Extreme time management is important, as all deadlines are to be reached to the betterment of each child and their family. Cover Letter – Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With experience in behavioral health, crisis support, and direct client services, I have developed a strong foundation in compassionate communication, active listening, and helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances. I am excited about the opportunity to bring these skills to an organization dedicated to supporting adolescents and their well-being.

My background includes working as a Registered Behavior Technician and providing intensive and respite services, where I support individuals with behavioral and developmental needs. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, remain patient under pressure, maintain professionalism, and approach each individual with empathy and respect. In addition, my work with DeafLEAD in a crisis-support role has reinforced the importance of building trust, responding thoughtfully to sensitive situations, and helping individuals feel heard during vulnerable moments.

I am currently working in a 100% remote position with DeafLEAD, which has provided me with direct experience managing professional responsibilities in a virtual work environment. I have a dedicated, private workspace equipped with the necessary technology, reliable high-speed internet, and the equipment needed to perform my duties effectively. I am confident in my ability to remain productive, communicate professionally, maintain confidentiality, and consistently complete my workload while working remotely. Transitioning into another fully virtual position would be a natural fit for my existing experience and established work environment.

I understand that the admissions process can be an important first step for families seeking behavioral health support for their children. I would approach this responsibility with compassion, organization, and attention to detail, ensuring that prospective families feel welcomed, informed, and supported as they explore available services. I am committed to creating positive first impressions, communicating clearly, and helping families navigate the admissions process with professionalism and sensitivity.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy by combining my behavioral health background, crisis-support experience, and established remote-work capabilities to support both families and the admissions team. I believe my commitment to helping others, adaptability, and ability to work independently would make me a valuable addition to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Serene Smith

candidates.cover_letter:
Scott Akers Sr., MA, M.Ed., MA, CSAC-S, QMHP
Greensboro, North Carolina

October 22, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Behavioral Health and Adolescent Services Opportunity

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 15 years of professional experience spanning behavioral health, adolescent counseling, family therapy, education, and human services, I bring a multidisciplinary background centered on helping young people and families overcome challenges, strengthen relationships, and achieve meaningful, sustainable progress.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with adolescents and families experiencing emotional and behavioral difficulties, substance use concerns, family conflict, academic challenges, and barriers to healthy development. My clinical experience includes implementing evidence-based approaches such as Brief Strategic Family Therapy (BSFT), Functional Family Therapy (FFT), Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI). These experiences have strengthened my ability to engage challenging populations, develop individualized interventions, coordinate services, and support positive behavioral outcomes.

Beyond direct clinical services, my background as an educator, college professor, and human services practitioner has equipped me with strong skills in communication, leadership, program development, psychoeducation, and interdisciplinary collaboration. I understand the importance of creating supportive environments where adolescents feel heard, families become active participants in treatment, and professionals work collaboratively toward shared goals.

What particularly attracts me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is its commitment to addressing adolescent mental health through compassionate, individualized, and family-centered care. I strongly believe that lasting behavioral change requires more than addressing immediate symptoms; it involves strengthening family systems, developing practical coping strategies, building resilience, and empowering young people to recognize their potential.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical knowledge, educational experience, leadership abilities, and commitment to adolescent wellness to your organization. I am confident that my diverse professional background would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team and the families you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional values align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Scott Akers Sr., MA, M.Ed., MA, CSAC-S, QMHP
Human Services Practitioner, Educator, and Communications Specialist

Stephenie Shelton

October 22, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in behavioral healthcare, a background in pediatric mental health crisis intervention, and a Master’s degree in healthcare administration, I bring a combination of clinical knowledge, communication skills, and administrative understanding that aligns with the needs of this position. I am passionate about helping adolescents and their families navigate the process of accessing appropriate mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Mental Health Technician at SUN Behavioral Health in Erlanger, Kentucky, I work in a behavioral healthcare environment where patient safety, communication, confidentiality, and collaboration are essential. This experience has strengthened my understanding of behavioral health services and the importance of creating a supportive environment for individuals experiencing emotional and psychological challenges. I have developed the ability to remain professional in stressful situations, communicate effectively with members of an interdisciplinary team, and recognize the importance of treating every patient with dignity and respect.

Previously, I served as a Behavioral Health Specialist in the Emergency Department at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, where I supported children and adolescents experiencing mental health crises. This experience gave me valuable insight into the challenges families face when seeking behavioral health services for their children. It also strengthened my understanding of the importance of timely access to care, clear communication, and collaboration among healthcare professionals. I recognize that connecting families with the appropriate level of treatment requires compassion, patience, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate sensitive information in a professional and supportive manner.

My Master’s degree in healthcare administration has further prepared me to contribute to the operational and coordination responsibilities of an admissions role. Through my education, I have developed a stronger understanding of healthcare systems, quality improvement, ethical decision-making, and the importance of efficient processes in supporting positive patient outcomes. I understand that an effective admissions process involves more than gathering information; it also requires helping families understand available services, coordinating next steps, maintaining accurate documentation, and communicating with appropriate team members to facilitate access to care.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines behavioral health, family engagement, and healthcare coordination. I would welcome the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate what can often be an overwhelming treatment-seeking process. I understand the importance of approaching these conversations without judgment, protecting confidential information, and helping families feel heard while ensuring their needs are communicated appropriately to the clinical team. I am also prepared to bring organization, accountability, and professionalism to a virtual work environment while maintaining a strong focus on responsiveness and service.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, educational background, and commitment to improving access to care could contribute to the admissions team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of helping adolescents and their families take meaningful steps toward treatment, recovery, and improved well-being.

Sincerely,
Stephenie Shelton

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC). With direct, hands-on experience in behavioral health and developmental disability settings—most recently at SUN Behavioral Kentucky and the Southwest Ohio Developmental Center—I bring a deep understanding of crisis de-escalation, clinical documentation, and client-centered intake support to this role.  
In my current work as a Mental Health Technician at SUN Behavioral Kentucky, I regularly serve as a critical bridge between patients entering the facility and the clinical team. I assist with the admissions and onboarding workflow by welcoming individuals on what is often their most vulnerable day, gathering critical background information, de-escalating heightened anxiety, and ensuring all intake records and vital observations are entered accurately and in full compliance with regulatory and HIPAA standards. Because I routinely manage crisis interventions and provide one-on-one emotional support, I excel at establishing immediate trust and communicating with clarity and warmth under pressure—skills essential for being the first voice an adolescent, parent, or adult hears when seeking PHP or IOP care.  
Prior to this, as a Therapeutic Program Worker at the Southwest Ohio Developmental Center, I maintained meticulous records of client progress, facilitated structured group sessions, and collaborated with multidisciplinary staff to carry out individualized treatment goals. These experiences honed my ability to manage workflows independently, maintain organized documentation across EHR/EMR platforms, and guide individuals systematically through multi-step care processes.  
Key qualifications I bring to your admissions pipeline include:
Admissions & Intake Facilitation: Hands-on experience collecting initial documentation, recording behavioral assessments, and guiding patients and family members through entry protocols with empathy and precision.  
Behavioral Health & Crisis Expertise: Proven ability to de-escalate distress, actively listen, and maintain a calm, reassuring demeanor with individuals facing mental health challenges and co-occurring disorders.  
Independent Organization & Follow-Through: Rigorous attention to documentation standards, pipeline follow-up, and protocol adherence, ensuring no inquiry or record slips through the cracks.  
I am prepared to immediately support your remote admissions team by converting incoming inquiries into reassuring, structured pathways to treatment.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Peer Support Specialist II position with Rutgers University Behavioral
Health Care’s 988 Lifeline Services. As a dedicated Peer Support and Recovery Services professional, Community Health
Worker, Family Peer Support Specialist, and Recovery Coach, I bring a diverse background in behavioral health, crisis
intervention, recovery-oriented support, healthcare navigation, and advocacy. I am passionate about meeting individuals
where they are, creating meaningful human connections, and ensuring that people experiencing emotional distress or
crisis feel heard, respected, supported, and empowered.
In my current role with Heartland Family Service, I provide individualized peer support, recovery coaching, crisis and
wellness planning, resource navigation, and advocacy for individuals experiencing mental health challenges, substance
use recovery, disabilities, and significant life transitions. My responsibilities include identifying immediate needs,
recognizing barriers to care, collaborating with behavioral health professionals, supporting the development of
person-centered recovery goals, and connecting individuals with appropriate community resources and services.
My professional background also includes patient advocacy, healthcare coordination, family support, and
community-based services. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate effectively with individuals
from diverse backgrounds, remain grounded during emotionally challenging situations, recognize when additional
intervention may be necessary, and respond with compassion while maintaining professional boundaries.
Throughout my career, I have pursued additional education and training in mental health first aid, Wellness Recovery
Action Planning (WRAP), trauma-informed care, emergency medical services, and supportive communication. These
experiences have provided me with a strong foundation in understanding the complex relationship between mental health,
physical health, trauma, disability, and the social determinants of health.
What particularly draws me to Rutgers University’s 988 Lifeline Services is the opportunity to offer meaningful support
during moments when a single conversation can make a profound difference. I believe effective peer support is not simply
about providing information or identifying solutions. It is about establishing trust, listening without judgment, honoring
individual experiences, and helping people recognize their strengths and available choices.
I recognize the importance of balancing empathy with sound judgment, appropriate assessment, accurate documentation,
confidentiality, and established crisis response protocols. I am comfortable working independently, collaborating with
interdisciplinary teams, and using technology to coordinate and document services.
I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, dedication, and recovery-oriented perspective to Rutgers
University Behavioral Health Care. I am especially interested in supporting the mission of the 988 Lifeline by helping
individuals feel less alone, increasing access to appropriate resources, and promoting hope, dignity, and connection during
times of crisis.
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my professional background,
training, and commitment to peer support align with the needs of your team. 


Sincerely 
Crystl McCall

October 21, 2026

Dear Hiring Team,

I believe the person answering that first phone call can make all the difference in whether someone takes the next step toward getting help. That is what caught my attention about this opportunity. You're not simply looking for someone to answer calls and schedule appointments. You're looking for someone who can recognize the importance of that moment, connect with the person on the other end of the phone, and help them move forward. That is exactly the kind of work I enjoy doing.

I bring a combination of remote admissions experience, behavioral health support, and genuine compassion for people who are navigating difficult circumstances. During my time with Ultimate Medical Academy, I worked remotely in admissions, interviewing prospective students, managing a high volume of inquiries, maintaining CRM records, and following up with individuals throughout the enrollment process. I ranked number one in my division and achieved 380% of my enrollment target. Those results came from more than meeting performance expectations. I understood how to build relationships, listen to people's needs, address their concerns, and remain consistent in my follow-through.

What makes my background especially relevant is that I also understand the importance of emotional support. Through my work with Youth Villages and my experience in family support counseling, I've worked with individuals and families facing behavioral challenges, emotional difficulties, and circumstances that require patience, compassion, and sound judgment. I've learned that people do not always know how to communicate what they need, especially when they're overwhelmed. Sometimes you have to listen beyond the initial question to understand how you can actually help.

I recognize that behavioral health admissions are different from educational admissions. Families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be frightened, exhausted, or uncertain about what happens next. I would approach those conversations with the same care I would want someone to show my own family, while ensuring that inquiries, documentation, referrals, and follow-ups are handled professionally and accurately.

I'm comfortable working independently in a remote environment, managing multiple conversations and responsibilities, maintaining confidential information, and following through until the next step is clear. I would welcome the opportunity to learn your admissions processes and become a dependable part of the team supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

I am confident in what I bring to this position, but what matters most to me is the opportunity to use my experience in a way that genuinely impacts someone's life. I would love the opportunity to speak with you about how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Inez D. Kearse

Dear Hiring Team,
I would like to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Masters of Social Work degree expected in January of 2027 and several years of experience in behavioral health, crisis services, client advocacy, and family support, I am passionate about helping individuals and families navigate difficult moments and connect with the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my background, values, and experience could support your admissions team.

Sydney Ramberg

candidates.cover_letter:
Sheila Boussiquot
Brandon, Florida
857-249-2752 | Sboussiquot@gmail.com

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy & Principles Recovery Center

Subject: Application for Virtual Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in human services, behavioral health, case management, and program support, I understand how important it is to make people feel heard, supported, and understood, especially when they are reaching out for help during a difficult time. I would welcome the opportunity to use my experience and compassion to help individuals and families navigate the admissions process and connect with the care they need.

Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals facing a variety of challenges, including mental health concerns, developmental disabilities, and housing instability. As an Engagement Partner II and Assistant Program Manager at Bay Cove Human Services, I supported individuals in their recovery journeys using approaches such as Motivational Interviewing and trauma-informed care. These experiences strengthened my communication skills, taught me the importance of meeting people where they are, and helped me develop the patience and understanding needed to support individuals through challenging situations.

My experience as a Stabilization Housing Case Manager at the New England Center and Home for Veterans also strengthened my ability to conduct intakes, maintain accurate records, coordinate services, and manage confidential client information. I understand the importance of organization, attention to detail, and protecting sensitive information in a healthcare setting. I believe these skills would translate well to managing admissions inquiries, maintaining accurate information in electronic health records and CRM systems, and helping ensure a smooth process for prospective clients and their families.

In my role as a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) Float, I developed the ability to build rapport quickly, adapt to different situations, and work effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds. I also bring experience working independently, managing responsibilities, and staying organized in fast-paced environments. Whether I am answering questions, explaining treatment options such as partial hospitalization (PHP) and intensive outpatient (IOP) programs, or coordinating the next steps in the admissions process, I would approach every interaction with professionalism, empathy, and a genuine desire to help.

What interests me most about this opportunity is the chance to make a positive difference from the very first point of contact. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can feel overwhelming for individuals and their families. I would take pride in helping make that first step a little easier by providing clear information, listening without judgment, and ensuring each caller feels respected and supported.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background in behavioral health, client advocacy, and case management could contribute to your admissions team. I look forward to the possibility of joining your organization and helping individuals and families take the next step toward recovery and wellness.

Sincerely,
Sheila Boussiquot

I am writing to express my interest in a counseling or behavioral health position within your organization. As a mental health professional with extensive experience in substance use disorder treatment, behavioral health, crisis intervention, healthcare,
rehabilitation, and client-centered services, I bring a well-rounded clinical background and a strong commitment to supporting individuals throughout treatment and recovery. I earned my Bachelor’s Degree in Clinical Psychology from Alabama A&M University in 2018 and my Master’s Degree in Counseling and Psychology from the University of West Alabama in 2020. I am currently completing my second master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Liberty University, with an anticipated
graduation date of December 2026, and anticipate obtaining my Associate Licensed Counselor (ALC) credential by February 2027. My education and clinical training have strengthened my skills in assessment, treatment planning, therapeutic intervention,
documentation, case conceptualization, crisis response, and evidence-informed care. My professional background includes more than 15 years of customer and consumer service experience, approximately 10 years of teaching and mentoring within special education, four years of administrative and management-related experience, four years of supervision and professional training, more than two years in hospital medical settings, extensive experience in clinical and behavioral health environments, and approaching five years of experience in substance use therapy and counseling. I have worked with children, adolescents, young adults, and adults across special education,
hospital, psychiatric, outpatient, and substance use treatment settings. My experience also includes psychiatric emergency intake, crisis intervention, court advocacy and liaison services for psychiatric patients, counseling, treatment coordination, and
interdisciplinary collaboration. For approximately five years, my professional focus has included substance use disorder treatment within both metropolitan and rural communities. I have provided services to adolescents and adults at various stages of recovery, including individuals experiencing co-occurring mental health concerns. This work has strengthened my ability to establish therapeutic rapport, promote treatment engagement, identify barriers to recovery, facilitate behavioral change, maintain clinical documentation, and provide individualized support based on each client’s needs. My clinical approach incorporates person-centered therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behavior
Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing (MI), and holistic approaches to care. I believe effective counseling requires treating

I strive to provide compassionate, ethical, and professional care while maintaining appropriate clinical boundaries. Throughout my career, I have developed strong communication, critical thinking, organization, problem-solving, time management, and leadership skills. I

Erin L. Johnson

Dear Admissions Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a dedicated human services professional with an Associate of Science in Human Services (graduated Magna Cum Laude) and ongoing Social Work studies, I have spent my career preparing to be the compassionate, clear voice that families need on some of the hardest days of their lives.

While my background is rooted in case coordination, database management, and family support, the workflows I have managed across diverse organizational structures directly mirror your admissions needs. Through my direct hands-on experience with The Learning Center for the Deaf, independent framing environments, and the Department of Children and Families, I have routinely navigated sensitive public sector databases to securely analyze, cross-reference, and process 20+ complex community resource files per week for families undergoing critical transitions. These roles taught me how to manage a high-volume digital pipeline independently while maintaining strict accuracy, compliance, and procedural focus. My practical administrative background ensures that I can rapidly adapt to your internal workflows and master your CRM and EMR systems, including Kipu.

Communication and accessibility are at the heart of everything I do. I am fully trilingual in English, Spanish, and American Sign Language. Utilizing a seamless, high-speed ASL Video Relay Service setup, I can efficiently field inbound calls, screen for program fit, and explain complex treatment options in plain, caring language to diverse populations with zero delay. Managing my current university curriculum entirely online has also proven my ability to drive my own pipeline and maintain strong follow-through in a fully remote environment.
I am incredibly motivated by AWA and PRC's family-centered, evidence-based approach to healing. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my screening skills, technical aptitude, and multilingual capabilities can help connect more families to your life-changing care.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Edlanda Delorme

Donavon Grier

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. Throughout my career in case management, higher education, crisis response, and community outreach, I have dedicated myself to helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances and access the support they need. Your commitment to providing adolescents with a safe, compassionate, and supportive environment strongly resonates with both my professional experience and personal values.

My experience as a Pretrial Officer for Bexar County further developed my ability to manage complex caseloads, assess individual circumstances, maintain accurate documentation, and connect individuals with community resources. Previously, as a police dispatcher and 911 operator, I learned to remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly during emergencies, and respond to sensitive situations with sound judgment. My commitment to helping vulnerable populations also extends into my community involvement. Through Ferro Family Ministries, our family's nonprofit organization, I have collaborated with churches and community volunteers across Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Mexico to support underserved youth and families. Our outreach efforts have included helping individuals access basic necessities, coordinating charitable assistance, and organizing fundraising initiatives for families facing significant hardships. These experiences reinforced my belief that meaningful support begins with listening, understanding individual needs, and treating every person with dignity and respect.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy's focus on supporting teenagers and their families through challenging periods in their lives. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With my professional background in substance use treatment and behavioral health, combined with my experience using Kipu and providing services through telehealth, I believe I would bring a valuable combination of clinical knowledge, technical proficiency, and compassion to your admissions team.

Throughout my career as a substance use disorder therapist and behavioral health professional, I have worked extensively with individuals experiencing addiction, co-occurring mental health conditions, trauma, and other complex challenges. My experience spans residential treatment, Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP), and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP). This familiarity with multiple levels of care allows me to explain treatment options confidently, recognize individual needs, and help prospective clients and their families navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I also have hands-on experience with Kipu electronic medical records, clinical documentation, treatment coordination, and telehealth services. I understand the importance of accurate recordkeeping, confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and timely communication in ensuring continuity of care. My clinical background has also strengthened my ability to work independently, prioritize responsibilities, and collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams.

Perhaps my greatest strength is my ability to connect with people, particularly during vulnerable or emotionally difficult moments. I understand that individuals reaching out for treatment may be frightened, hesitant, or unsure where to begin. I believe the first interaction with a treatment provider should communicate compassion, reassurance, and hope while offering clear, practical guidance toward the next step.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to use my clinical experience in a different but equally meaningful capacity. I recognize that the admissions process is often the beginning of someone's recovery journey, and I would find tremendous purpose in helping individuals and families access the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, familiarity with Kipu, and commitment to compassionate, client-centered care could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Chloé

candidates.summary: Office Administrator with experience in scheduling, front desk support, customer service, records management, payroll support, and daily office operations in a healthcare setting. Skilled in eCW, Microsoft Office, data entry, phone systems, and administrative coordination within healthcare and community service settings. Seeking an office administrative position where I can utilize my organizational, communication, patient support, and customer service skills to support efficient day-to-day operations. ?

work_history.title: Behavioral Health Care Coordinator Assistant
work_history.summary: Coordinate patient scheduling, intake support, and referral follow-up to facilitate timely access to services. Provide front desk and customer service support to patients and visitors in person and by phone, email and chat. Maintain electronic records, scan and organize documentation, and document patient encounters in eCW. Support daily administrative operations while handling confidential patient information Obtain patient demographic information and collect and verify insurance

work_history.title: Agency Administrative Assistant
work_history.company_name: Area IV Agency on Aging and Community Action Programs
work_history.summary: Managed front desk activity, greeted visitors, and directed clients to correct departments. Maintained calendars, prepared documents, scheduled meetings, and managed all fax, email, and telephonic communications. Provided administrative and customer service support to clients and staff.

work_history.title: Program Intake Specialist
work_history.company_name: Area IV Agency on Aging and Community Action Programs
work_history.summary: Assisted clients with applications and scheduled appointments for community-based services. Answered phones, returned voicemails, emails, chat messaging, and confidentially maintained office documentation. Supported outreach events and daily front-office operations.

work_history.title: Sales Manager
work_history.summary: Supervised office operations, employee scheduling, and payroll processing. Maintained records, completed audits, and supported staff training. Provided customer service and resolved account questions. Maintained and prepared profit and loss statemnts

October 21, 2026
Hiring Coordination Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy 
RE: Opportunity at Adolescent Wellness Academy
Dear Hiring Coordination Team,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the remote opportunity with the Adolescent
Wellness Academy. While my educational background utilizes a professional equivalence
model developed through over 20 years of hands-on experience, I bring a specialized
combination of real-world public safety dispatching, acute psychiatric clinical care, and a deep
understanding of remote crisis management. I am highly motivated to bring this background to
your organization to provide structured, empathetic, and trauma-informed care to the
populations you serve.
My professional foundation directly mirrors the high-acuity demands of behavioral health and
safety monitoring workflows. As a Deputy Sheriff Communications Specialist and 911
Dispatcher, I spent years managing critical emergency lines, conducting rapid risk
assessments, and navigating complex database networks under extreme pressure. I am
intimately familiar with real-time protocol adherence, strict confidentiality, and managing highstakes situations calmly and efficiently.
Complementing my public safety background is my direct clinical experience as a Patient
Care Technician in a high-acuity Psychiatric Unit at Ascension Saint Thomas. In this role, I
mastered nonviolent verbal crisis de-escalation, monitored patient behavior, and maintained
meticulous,HIPAA-compliantdigitaldocumentationduringcriticalsafetyincidents.
Additionally, my recent experience managing remote communication workflows and multichannel support for United Healthcare has sharpened my ability to deliver high-level virtual
assistance and maintain data integrity seamlessly.
I am fully equipped to meet all technical requirements for a remote operations position,
including maintaining a secure, dedicated workspace. I bring the technical proficiency,operational stamina, and emotional resilience required to handle sensitive documentation,
forms, and crisis communications effectively from day one.
Thank you for your time, consideration, and dedication to expanding accessible behavioral
health support. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my public safety, virtual
support, and psychiatric care background can serve the Adolescent Wellness Academy.
Sincerely,
Vivian Cherie Orlando

candidates.summary: Experienced remote customer service and patient-care professional with 15+ years across behavioral health support, intake-related services, crisis de-escalation, and emergency communications. work_history.title: Senior Customer Service Representative
work_history.summary: * Managed complex and sensitive healthcare inquiries through phone, email, and chat using compassionate de-escalation * Maintained accurate, secure client records and documented every interaction in compliance with privacy policies * Translated technical healthcare information into clear, actionable guidance for clients and families * Streamlined ticketing and communication workflows to support timely follow-up and consistent issue resolution * Coached representatives on customer engagement, troubleshooting, documentation, and service standards

work_history.title: Practice Manager
work_history.summary: * Served as a primary client contact, answering questions, resolving concerns, and coordinating appropriate next steps * Trained front-office staff on client intake, service communication, documentation, and satisfaction standards * Prepared client invoices, processed over-the-counter sales, and maintained accurate administrative records * Directed front-office operations while coordinating staff coverage, clinic workflows, and end-of-day closing * Maintained inventory records and tracked grant usage through organized documentation and cross-functional coordination

work_history.title: Patient Care Technician
work_history.summary: * Supported patients in a high-acuity adult behavioral health unit using trauma-informed crisis intervention and deescalation * Monitored patients at risk of self-harm or elopement through scheduled safety checks and continuous observation * Documented changes in mood, speech, behavior, and physical activity for timely clinical team review * Maintained a therapeutic, safe environment while communicating urgent behavioral changes to clinical staff

work_history.title: Assistant Manager Front Desk Clerk
work_history.summary: * Delivered welcoming front-desk service while answering inquiries, resolving complaints, and coordinating guest needs * Managed reservations and administrative records with accuracy across a high-volume hospitality environment * Coordinated large events and communicated details across departments to ensure reliable execution * Supported operations for an 87-room facility through clerical duties and customer follow-through

work_history.title: Deputy Sheriff Communications Officer
work_history.summary: * Answered and assessed high-stakes 911 calls, gathering essential information through active listening and questioning * Coordinated police, fire, and EMS responses while communicating clearly with callers and emergency personnel * Used CAD systems to track incidents and field units while maintaining accurate real-time operational records * Applied emergency dispatch protocols and provided clear pre-arrival instructions during active crises * Documented chronological call, radio, and incident details to support accountability and continuity * Monitored video feeds and alarm systems, initiating response procedures under established security protocols

work_history.title: Telecommunicator/Dispatcher
work_history.summary: * Answered 911 calls and gathered accurate information from individuals experiencing urgent or emergency situations * Screened and prioritized calls before coordinating police, fire, and emergency management responses * Entered and updated incident information in CAD, NCIC, TCIC, and TIES systems * Maintained clear communications with responders while documenting essential incident details

work_history.title: Office Manager
work_history.summary: * Served as a client liaison, answering questions, resolving concerns, and coordinating service-related follow-up * Prepared client invoices, managed accounts receivable and payable, and maintained accurate financial records * Trained front-office staff on administrative procedures, client communication, and documentation standards * Managed payroll, collections, inventory records, and routine office administration

candidates.cover_letter:
Good afternoon,
        I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I believe my combination of behavioral health quality assurance, nursing home intake, insurance verification, and remote work experience makes me a strong candidate for this role. I bring both the administrative skills needed to help move the admissions process forward and an understanding of the importance of treating individuals and families with compassion when they are seeking care.

In my current role with Vibrant Emotional Health, I review 988 crisis calls, chats, and texts to evaluate interaction quality, adherence to established protocols, risk assessment, and appropriate crisis response. This experience has strengthened my ability to recognize concerns, pay attention to important details, assess whether established procedures are followed, and understand the importance of appropriate responses in sensitive situations. Working in crisis services has also reinforced that the way people are treated when they reach out for help matters. I would bring that same level of care, attentiveness, and professionalism to conversations with adolescents and families exploring treatment options.

My previous experience in a nursing home setting also provided me with hands-on experience in intake and insurance verification. This background is particularly relevant to a position that requires gathering information, helping prospective clients navigate admissions requirements, and addressing insurance-related steps. I understand that an organized intake process requires accuracy, follow-through, and clear communication. I would use those skills to help families understand what to expect, identify the next steps in the admissions process, and move forward without unnecessary confusion.

I also bring experience working remotely, where independence, accountability, organization, and consistent communication are important. My quality assurance background has further developed my attention to detail and appreciation for accurate documentation and established procedures. I understand that admissions coordination involves more than answering inquiries; it requires keeping track of outstanding steps, following up appropriately, and helping ensure that people do not get lost in the process of seeking services.

As I pursue my Master of Social Work, I continue to strengthen my understanding of behavioral health, person-centered care, and the challenges individuals and families may face when trying to access support. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my administrative and behavioral health experience with my commitment to helping people connect with appropriate services. I would value the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate the admissions process with clarity, respect, and compassion while supporting the team’s efforts to maintain an organized and responsive admissions pipeline.

Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in intake, insurance verification, remote work, and behavioral health quality assurance could benefit Adolescent Wellness Academy and the families it serves.

Best regards,
Nycole Alexandre
