candidates.cover_letter:
Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
October 20, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent calls about a struggling teenager, or an adult finally reaches out about their substance use, the first voice they hear matters. I have spent more than 20 years being that voice, and I would love to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator.
My career has been built on admissions, assessment, and referral work. At National Healthcare Associates, I handled inbound referrals from several hospital systems at once for multiple facilities, screened each client against admission criteria, and decided whether to accept, deny, or refer them elsewhere. I verified benefits, secured Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial authorizations, and advocated directly with insurers to keep admissions from stalling. Before that, I spent 17 years as Regional Clinical Admissions Director for Kindred Healthcare, managing the full referral to admission cycle for adults with psychiatric and behavioral needs, including co-occurring drug and alcohol use disorders.
I am used to owning my pipeline without daily direction. At Kindred I independently ran a four-state territory, building relationships with case managers, social workers, and discharge planners both virtually and in person, and following up consistently until every referral had a clear outcome. That work generated enough admissions that the organization opened additional units and a new facility. I am comfortable working in CRM and EMR systems, including EPIC, Navi, and Allscripts, and I keep accurate, HIPAA-compliant records.
I also bring a counselor's foundation. I hold an M.S. in Mental Health Counseling and an M.S.Ed. in School Counseling from Syracuse University, my early clinical work included adolescents in day treatment and residential programs, and I served as board president of YouthHarbor. As a Reiki Master Teacher and owner of Beehive Wellness, I meet people in difficult moments with calm and compassion, which is exactly how I would greet your callers.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families and adults move from that first call to a clear next step. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Keli Scott

Dear Hiring Manager,

	I am writing to express my interest in your Virtual Admission Coordinator position through Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a strong background in research and clinical work, I am confident I can contribute effectively to your team through my administrative knowledge, interpersonal skills, compassion, knowledge of substance use and mental health, and data collection experience.

	My bachelor’s degree in psychology from Clemson University has given me the skills to apply statistical analysis and clinical administrative work in my current and past positions. As a Research Assistant at the Medical University of South Carolina, I conduct 20 interviews weekly and record all data through REDCap, Box, and Excel. In these interviews, I lead with empathy and understanding when discussing each patient's circumstances and communicate with their therapist accordingly. While administering assessments during appointments, I ensure that I am clear with the participant about what is expected during our discussions and give them resources when necessary. Each week, I update all logs and REDCap to reflect new data and create weekly meeting agendas to update my team on participant recruitment and enrollment. I have excelled in maintaining IRB materials by submitting all amendments and continuing reviews. My current position highlights skills that I thoroughly enjoy, such as working with participants and conducting assessments, which is why I would be thrilled to apply these to this role.

	My previous role as a Registered Behavior Technician enabled me to focus on child therapy. I implemented Applied Behavior Analysis with patients aged four to sixteen. It was essential to be thoroughly versed in each client's clinical assessments, protocols, and behavioral functioning. Data collection was the main focus of this position, so I excelled at meeting each goal and collecting all necessary data points during each session. My data collection was thorough and exceeded expectations, achieving at least 80 percent each time for my client’s learning objective.

In my previous research at Clemson University, I strengthened my interpersonal skills by recruiting deaf and hearing individuals for my research project, which allowed me to receive feedback and learn more about emotion and cognition. I also practiced several assessments with other students to learn the proper language and resources to provide based on each individual's circumstances. My experience throughout school and in my current or past positions has given me thorough experience communicating with individuals about personal topics and finding them the right resources that are applicable. I believe these experiences align with the requirements of your virtual admissions coordinator position, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute them to your team. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you in greater detail.
Sincerely,
Megan Pfizenmayer

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

When I read about your commitment to creating a place where troubled teens and their families feel safe, loved, cared for, and no longer alone, it truly touched my heart. I believe every child deserves to feel supported, understood, and accepted, especially during some of the most challenging years of their lives. Adolescence can already be difficult, and when mental health challenges or substance use become part of that journey, having a compassionate support system can make a tremendous difference. This is one of the reasons I am so passionate about the opportunity to join Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Helping people has always been something that brings me a genuine sense of purpose. During my time as a Case Manager with Prevention Central, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals and families facing various challenges. I conducted assessments, developed individualized case plans, identified barriers, coordinated supportive services, and connected clients with community resources. What I enjoyed most was getting to know the individuals I served, listening to their concerns, understanding their circumstances, and working alongside them to find solutions. I learned that no two individuals are the same, and sometimes making a difference begins with simply taking the time to listen and showing someone that their situation matters.

I understand how important the first point of contact can be when a parent reaches out seeking help for their child. They may be frightened, overwhelmed, frustrated, or simply unsure of what to do next.  I believe the person answering that call has an opportunity to provide more than information. They can offer reassurance, compassion, and a sense of hope. I would never want a parent or teenager to feel like they are just another phone call or admission. I want them to feel heard, respected, and supported while helping them move toward the care they need.

In addition to my case management background, I worked remotely as an Intake Coordinator with All County Health Care, where I assisted clients through the intake process, gathered sensitive information, reviewed documentation, verified eligibility, coordinated services, and maintained confidential records. This experience strengthened my ability to work independently, manage multiple responsibilities, communicate professionally, and remain organized in a fast-paced environment. I understand that admissions require both compassion and urgency because individuals and families seeking treatment should not have to experience unnecessary delays in accessing care.

I am currently nearing completion of my Bachelor of Social Work, a goal that means a great deal to me because I know this is the field where my heart belongs. My training in Trauma-Informed Care, Motivational Interviewing, Mental Health First Aid, and suicide prevention has further strengthened my commitment to meeting people where they are and treating every individual with dignity and understanding. Although my direct admissions experience has not been specifically within a substance use treatment facility, I bring years of transferable experience in intake, case management, client advocacy, and working with vulnerable populations. I am confident in my ability to learn your admissions processes and contribute positively to your team.

What resonates with me most about your mission is the belief that healing happens through connection, compassion, and community.  Families need to know they are not alone in navigating these challenges. While an Admissions Coordinator may not provide the treatment itself, I believe we play an important role in helping families take that first step toward healing.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to interview. I am not simply looking for another job. I am looking for an opportunity to continue making a difference in the lives of individuals and families

Sincerely,
Stacy Scott
 754-273-4930

October 20, 2026

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My experience reviewing behavioral health referrals, conducting intake assessments, coordinating with insurance representatives, and supporting adolescents and adults aligns closely with your programs. I would bring a compassionate, organized approach to helping callers understand their options and take the next step toward treatment.

In my current role as Program Supervisor and Utilization Review Specialist at Arizona Children’s Group, I review referrals for program acceptance and collaborate with families, case managers, clinicians, and insurance representatives to coordinate care for adolescents with mental health, substance use, and developmental needs. I use Kipu daily as our electronic medical record system, alongside other EHR platforms, to document and coordinate care. My utilization review responsibilities include participating in peer-to-peer reviews, communicating insurance approval and denial decisions, and maintaining records in accordance with state and insurance requirements.

Previously, as Program Supervisor at Dutiful Angels Behavioral Clinic, I conducted intake assessments in an intensive outpatient setting serving adults with varied mental health diagnoses, including many with serious mental illness. I also developed substance use recovery programming and worked with community resources and referral partners to expand services available to clients. This experience prepared me to gather relevant information, recognize individual treatment needs, and help people navigate available services.

My work with adolescents, adults, and families has taught me to listen carefully, communicate clearly, and remain patient when people are overwhelmed. I understand how much the first conversation can matter. I would bring that sensitivity to admissions calls, explain treatment options in accessible language, and maintain careful documentation and consistent follow-through throughout the admissions process.

With a Psy.D. and MSW, I bring clinical understanding, compassionate communication, and careful documentation to helping individuals and families navigate treatment options and next steps.

work_history.title: Program Supervisor Utilization Review Specialist
work_history.summary: Description of Site: Arizona Children's Group is a co-ed behavioral health program for male and female youth, ages 12-17, who require intensive residential community-based treatment for mental health, substance abuse, and/or disabilities. Our programs include therapeutic behavioral health, developmental disability treatment, and day services and treatment programs. Responsibilities: Review referrals for acceptance into the ACG program. Engage with clients and parents for coaching sessions. Facilitate groups on anger, self-esteem, and DBT. Communicate with parents, case managers, insurance representatives, school personnel and administrators, and outside groups to achieve the highest quality of wraparound services for each client. Review treatment plans to ensure therapeutic goals are being met, as well as to ensure goals are specific and measurable. Maintain records in compliance with state and insurance regulations. Engage in program development, incentive programs, and increasing parental engagement. Maintain company, staff, and client records according to state and insurance regulations. Comply and provide all information requested during state and insurance audits. Utilize numerous Electronic Health Records (EHR) programs to coordinate care with insurance companies, case managers, clinicians, nurses, and staff. Engage in Peer-to-Peer reviews to coordinate care for clients and engaged in research to deliver educated opinions of client's progress, prognosis, and length of stay. Report all approval and denial results to administration for review. Participates in conferences and networking functions to market the ACG program to community partners and referral sources, as well as to foster and strengthen current professional relationships to foster partnerships.

work_history.title: Program Supervisor
work_history.summary: Description of Site: Dutiful Angels is an Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) serving individuals with a variety of mental health diagnoses, psychosocial concerns, and substance abuse. We offer top-notch personalized support services, including individual and group therapy for individuals. We also have suboxone treatment plans for clients struggling with substance addiction. Since our establishment in 2018, we have been working towards proper disability care and advocacy, helping eliminate the stigma against people with these disorders and substance abuse issues. Our team is always committed to delivering high standard and flexible intervention strategies that can address all of our client's needs. Responsibilities: Conduct intake assessments. Develop program recovery program for patient's suffering from substance abuse. Train bachelors level clinicians on recovery strategies, retention methods, gaining clinical insights, and proper documentation methods. Review case notes and provide feedback to BHTs in a supervisory role. Engage with community resources to expand services offered to clients. Train new staff on company rules, regulations, and protocols. Maintain company, staff, and client records to maintain compliance with state and insurance regulations. Comply and provide all information requested during state and insurance audits. Participates in conferences and networking functions to market the Dutiful Angeles IOP to community partners and referral sources, as well as to foster and strengthen current professional relationships to foster partnerships.

work_history.title: Clinical Psychologist
work_history.summary: Description of Site: Arizona Children's Group is a co-ed behavioral health program for male and female youth, ages 12-17, who require intensive residential community-based treatment for mental health or disabilities. Our programs include therapeutic behavioral health, developmental disability treatment, and day services and treatment programs. Responsibilities: Conduct both individual and family therapy sessions that include trauma-processing for all residents. Engage in crisis work. Conduct psychological evaluations related to diagnostic formulation and juvenile psychosexual evaluations when necessary. Participate in IEP meetings with residents. Engaged in program development, building incentive programs, and increasing parental engagement.

work_history.title: Owner of Private Practice Clinical Psychologist
work_history.summary: Description of Site: Brain Behavior, PC provides psychotherapy in the form of individual, couples', family, and groups for several populations including children, adolescents, and adults. We also specialize in conducting psychological evaluations and psychosexual evaluations in both the private and forensic realms. Responsibilities: Conduct individual, family, and couples therapy on a variety of issues but specializing in trauma-based difficulties. Conduct psychological testing related to diagnostic formulation, child custody and DCS related evaluations, and juvenile psychosexual evaluations.

work_history.title: Clinical Psychologist Clinical Supervisor Program Administrator
work_history.summary: Glendale, Arizona Position: Clinical Psychologist, Clinical Supervisor, Program Administrator Description of Site: McGady and Associates Psychological Services (MAAPS) provides a variety of clinical, forensic, consultation, supervision, and training services to the greater phoenix area. Clinical services include individual, couples', family, and group psychotherapy for children, adolescents, adults, and geriatrics. Psychological evaluations are provided to assist with diagnostic clarification and treatment planning. Also conducts comprehensive and psychosexual evaluations. MAAPS provides psychotherapy services from a variety of theoretical perspectives and modalities and selects the best approach that fits with the patient's needs, culture, background, and situation. Forensic services include psychological evaluations for criminal and family courts such as risk assessments, mitigation, competency, parenting, bonding, severance, veteran and disability determination. Dr. McGady provides consultation services for the public, private and government sectors, and supervisory services for mental health providers at both the Master's and Doctoral levels. Dr. McCall provides individual therapy, psychodiagnostic evaluations, psychosexual evaluations, forensic related evaluations. Responsibilities: Conduct individual, couples, and group therapy on issues related to alcohol and substance abuse and dependence, marital discord, infidelity, trust and intimacy, mood disorders, other Axis I disorders, and personality disorders. Conduct extensive psychological testing related to diagnostic formulation, pain management evaluations, bariatric surgery evaluations, child custody and CPS related evaluations, and forensic evaluations.

work_history.title: Doctoral Psychology Intern
work_history.company_name: Centerstone Hospital and Addiction Center/Centerstone Consortium
work_history.summary: Bradenton, Florida Supervisor: Dr. Bob Boxley, PhD. Position: Doctoral Psychology Intern Description of Site: The Centerstone Consortium is comprised of three sites including Centerstone (Centerstone Hospital and Addiction Center, Centerstone Outpatient, Centerstone Testing Center), Jewish Family & Children's Service (JFCS), and AllCare. Centerstone is one of the nation's largest non-profit behavioral health organizations with locations spanning across 5 states. This site located in Bradenton, FL serves over 16,000 clients annually. Mental health and substance abuse issues with adults, adolescents and children are handled in an evidence-based manner. Inpatient therapy, outpatient therapy, trauma-informed care, co-occurring therapy and general child/adult assessment are common here. Jewish Family & Children's Service is a multi-function family agency serving The Suncoast of Florida. The services are based on the premise that personnel trained in understanding the behavior and environments of individuals, can help them with crises, problems, and growth issues to improve the quality of their lives. AllCare is a family-owned organization is committed to delivering the finest possible health care to patients of all ages, from newborn to active aging adults. As a medical psychology placement, AllCare aspires to develop longterm physician- patient relationships and foster preventative and educational care for clients across the lifespan. The Centerstone Hospital (formerly Manatee Glens Hospital) is an APA-Accredited internship site providing psychiatric and other mental health services for adults. Group therapy, individual and family therapy, as well as medication management, are available to facilitate the individual's return to the home. The hospital is a caring and safe place that provides 24-hour medical monitoring. In the Centerstone Addiction Center, Centerstone provides detox services to adults and teens struggling with addiction and require medical supervision to safe and comfortable detox. While participating in services, patients receive a medical exam and lab work. Individual, group and family programming focuses on education that targets the addiction process, stages of change, motivation to change, identification of relapse triggers, family dynamics and continued sobriety. Sober fun and leisure are part of recovery. Centerstone specializes in cooccurring mental health and trauma care. The Centerstone Crisis Center provides intensive treatment for children and adolescents who have emotional disorders, as well as providing a temporary safe place with crisis stabilization services for adults and their families. Centerstone physicians examine and determine appropriate treatments for each patient. Group therapy, individual and family therapy, as well as medication management, help facilitate the individual's return home. Responsibilities: Conducted psychodiagnostic assessments on adults, children, and adolescents. Conducted individual, group, and family therapies with patients residing in the hospital, crisis (adult and child) and 28- day addictions units. Group therapy topics include grounding skills, coping skills, art therapy, toxic relationships, codependency, anger management, understanding my diagnosis, substance abuse, boundaries, and issues related to LGBTQ. Individual treatment goals include sobriety maintenance, symptom reduction, family reunification, self-esteem building, acceptance, and increase in parenting skills. Patients are diverse in terms of diagnosis (Bipolar I and II, ADHD, PTSD, Substance Dependence, Schizophrenia, Schizophreniform Disorder, Schizotypal Disorder, Intellectual Disability, Learning Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Reactive Attachment Disorder, Conduct Disorder, Oppositional Defiant Disorder, Antisocial Personality Disorder, Borderline Personality Disorder, and Histrionic Personality Disorder), age, race, gender, SES, sexual orientation, and gender identity.

work_history.title: Licensed Master Social Worker
work_history.summary: Description of Site: Moving On Life Center, Inc. is comprised of credentialed counselors, psychotherapists, and wellness consultants take a holistic approach to individual and family counseling by treating the cause, not just the symptoms. Moving On Life Center, Inc. provides in-home, school and community services to children, teens, adults, and families. Adolescent treatment involves meeting with a counselor to help work through challenges they might experience as a result of peer pressure, family conflict, lack of self-esteem, or substance abuse problems. During family treatment we strive to get as many family members to sit down and express themselves to help others be heard. This can include grief issues, separation issues, or issues if the dynamics of the family have changed. Individual therapy is provided for people faced with the problems such as anxiety and depression. This service is for couples that are experiencing trouble in their marriage or their relationships based on a lack of communication. Couples are taught ways to communicate more effectively with one another so each partner can be heard. Responsibilities: Conducted in-home therapy with children, adolescents, family members, case managers, and other treatment team members. Treatment goals included managing problematic behaviors, self-esteem building, building coping skills, and symptom reduction.

work_history.title: Licensed Master Social Worker
work_history.summary: Description of Site: People Empowering People of Arizona is a community-based clinic serving patient's receiving state funded Medicaid with various psychological disorders. Clients are diverse in terms of age, gender, socioeconomic status, gender, disability, and diagnosis. Responsibilities: Provided in-home counseling to adults with varying disorders aimed at providing patients with adaptive coping skills, building self-esteem and self-confidence, substance abuse counseling, instilling and maintaining boundaries, effective and positive communication skills, and psychoeducation. Completed daily progress notes and billing sheets, and monthly reports on progress towards patient's identified treatment goals.

work_history.title: Psychometrician
work_history.summary: Description of Site: The psychologists of Affiliated Psychological Professionals evaluate individuals, couples, and families in educational, intellectual, mental health, career, and forensic areas. Evaluations range from simple career assessments to comprehensive psychological testing, diagnosis, and feedback. Responsibilities: Administer and score juvenile forensic evaluations for youth mandated by the Mesa Department of Juvenile Probation. Assessment instruments include KBIT-2, Draw-a-Person projective measure, WRAT-4, WICS-IV, Rotter Sentence Completion Test, and BASC-2. Complete clinical interviews with parent/DCS caseworker/legal guardians.

work_history.title: Mental Health Clinician
work_history.summary: Description of Site: Desert Edge Mentoring Services is an outpatient clinic that serves a diverse population by addressing the growing needs of its transitioned aged youth and their adult parents. Interventions are designed to be flexible, client-centered, family-focused, and culturally responsive for evidence-based outcomes. Clients are referred by the Department of Children and Families (DCS) and are mandated to attend 20 hours of individual and/or couples therapy to achieve reunification with children removed by DCS for negligent parenting. Responsibilities: Conduct individual, couples, and group therapy with clients involved with DCS. Therapy sessions focus on co-parenting independent living skills domestic independency coping skills for anger management life skills appropriate social interactions confidence and self-esteem building and the impacts of substance abuse and domestic violence on children. Also provide case management through assisting clients with educational support services FASFA assistance and referrals to community resources.

Hiring Manager

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescence Wellness Academy. With over three years of experience in behavioral health admissions, client assessments, insurance verification, treatment coordination, and patient intake, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of compassionate, efficient, and individualized care. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, professionalism, and dedication to your team and contribute to helping adolescents and their families access the support and treatment they need.

In my current role as Lead Day Time Admissions Coordinator at Archstone Behavioral Health, I oversee the admissions process from the initial inquiry through enrollment. My responsibilities include verifying insurance benefits, conducting comprehensive assessments and screenings, identifying potential substance use disorders, and helping determine appropriate levels of care. I also coordinate travel arrangements, maintain accurate and confidential client records, and collaborate with probation officers and court officials when coordinating mandated treatment services. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, communicate effectively with individuals and families during difficult circumstances, and ensure a smooth and supportive admissions experience.

My previous experience as an Admissions Coordinator with Magnolia Ranch Recovery and Genesis Detox further developed my skills in client communication, treatment coordination, documentation, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams to support individualized treatment planning. In addition, my experience as a Customer Service Manager strengthened my leadership, problem-solving, organization, and conflict-resolution skills. I understand the importance of building trust, responding to concerns with empathy, maintaining confidentiality, and helping people navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I believe my combination of behavioral health admissions experience, strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and compassionate approach would make me a valuable addition to Adolescence Wellness Academy. I am especially interested in the opportunity to apply my experience in a setting focused on supporting adolescents and their families, where clear communication, patience, and a commitment to quality care are essential.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to behavioral health can contribute to the mission of Adolescence Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Allison Bertolino

candidates.cover_letter:
October 21, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Master of Science in Criminal Behavior, a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare administration, family services, and the legal field, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills that I believe would translate well into this position. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents, adults, and families as they navigate the process of seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

During my time at Bellbrook Family Practice, I gained extensive experience communicating with patients, coordinating appointments, managing medical records, and serving as a point of contact between patients, healthcare providers, and pharmacies. I regularly handled high volumes of phone calls, responded to patient inquiries, coordinated paperwork, and maintained sensitive medical information. This experience taught me the importance of patience, accuracy, confidentiality, and clear communication, particularly when assisting individuals who may be experiencing uncertainty or frustration.

Additionally, my internship with the Greene County Family Visitation Center allowed me to work directly with children and families navigating challenging circumstances. Through supervised visitation services, behavioral observations, and court-related documentation, I developed a greater understanding of the importance of providing compassionate, nonjudgmental support while maintaining professional boundaries. My current position with the Montgomery County Prosecutor’s Office has further strengthened my ability to manage confidential information, maintain detailed records, and balance multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced professional environment.

My graduate education has also provided me with a deeper understanding of psychological disorders, substance use, behavioral health assessment, and the social and environmental factors that influence mental health. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be an overwhelming experience, particularly for adolescents and families who may be unfamiliar with the process. I would welcome the opportunity to help make that first interaction a positive one by providing clear information, reassurance, and consistent follow-through.

I am enthusiastic about the possibility of contributing to an organization dedicated to making behavioral healthcare more accessible. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my educational background, healthcare experience, and commitment to supporting individuals and families could contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,
Madelyn Gilpin

Hiring Selection Committee

Subject: Application for Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
Dear Members of the Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Master of Science in Special Education/ABA, a Bachelor’s degree in Sociology, and extensive experience managing adolescent mental health and substance use challenges within Indiana communities, I am uniquely prepared to guide families through the critical first steps of their healing journey.
In my current role as a High School and Community-Based Care Specialist at Centerstone of Indiana, I work daily on the frontlines of youth mental health. I actively coordinate care plans, conduct client interviews, and deliver crisis interventions for adolescents navigating severe personal and emotional challenges. This role requires a high degree of empathy, rapid clinical problem-solving, and a deep understanding of behavioral health—qualities that are essential when answering an inquiry from a parent or teenager in crisis. Furthermore, my previous tenure at L.A.S.E.R. Project Inc. allowed me to support families heavily impacted by substance abuse and mental health adjustment issues, giving me a comprehensive perspective on the systemic support systems these youth require.
The "virtual" aspect of this coordinator role aligns seamlessly with my entrepreneurial background. As the former owner and life coach at Bennett and Hutson, I successfully operated a fully remote, global coaching practice. I am highly adept at utilizing virtual communication tools, managing digital scheduling systems, and establishing immediate, cross-cultural rapport with clients across varying time zones, including the US, UK, and Australasia. I know how to create a warm, welcoming, and structured environment through a digital screen or phone call, ensuring that anxious families feel heard, validated, and safely guided.
Additionally, I bring a robust administrative toolkit, including specialized knowledge of individualized assessments, state compliance frameworks, and active clinical certifications such as CANS 6+ / ANSA and Psychological First Aid. I understand the vital importance of accurate data collection during the admissions process to ensure seamless transition into active treatment.
I am incredibly drawn to the Adolescent Wellness Academy’s holistic mission to treat adolescent mental health and substance use. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical insight, virtual operational experience, and passion for youth advocacy can serve your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Miggin M. Hutson, M.S.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the **Virtual Admissions Coordinator: Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment** position. With my  experience supporting individuals with behavioral health needs and mental illness, I am confident that my clinical support skills, compassion, communication abilities, and dedication to patient care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my previous role at a 140-bed private psychiatric hospital, I provided care and support to adult patients ranging from geriatric individuals to returning veterans. Working under the direction of nursing and medical staff, I helped patients adjust to new routines, participate in social and therapeutic activities, and complete daily living tasks. I monitored patient behavior, maintained appropriate boundaries, assessed safety concerns, and responded effectively to crisis situations, including assisting with restraints when necessary to prevent injury.

In addition to my direct patient-care experience, I have developed strong skills in behavioral health referrals, admissions, and intake coordination. I am comfortable answering inbound calls and responding to inquiries from clients, parents and guardians, families, referral sources, and healthcare providers. I communicate with patience, empathy, and professionalism while gathering essential information, identifying immediate concerns, and helping families understand available treatment options.

I am familiar with explaining Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP) in clear, caring, and easy-to-understand language. I understand that families seeking adolescent mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing significant stress, and I approach each interaction with sensitivity, respect, and a nonjudgmental attitude. I can help families understand program expectations, levels of care, next steps, and the admissions process while ensuring that urgent safety concerns are communicated promptly to the appropriate clinical staff.

My additional qualifications include:

- Answering inbound calls and responding professionally to inquiries from adolescents, parents, guardians, families, providers, and referral sources  
- Gathering accurate demographic, clinical, insurance, and referral information during initial conversations  
- Screening prospective clients for program fit based on presenting concerns, treatment needs, age, safety considerations, and level of care  
- Explaining PHP, IOP, mental health, and substance use treatment services in a clear and compassionate manner  
- Recognizing potential safety concerns and escalating urgent situations according to established protocols  
- Verifying insurance eligibility and benefits and assisting with authorization-related information  
- Coordinating clinical assessments, intake appointments, admission dates, and required paperwork  
- Communicating with families, providers, clinicians, and other members of the treatment team to support a smooth admissions process  
- Following up consistently with every caller until the individual is scheduled, connected with services, or appropriately referred elsewhere  
- Maintaining accurate and timely documentation in CRM and electronic medical record systems  
- Entering referral and admissions information accurately while protecting confidential patient information  
- Completing documentation in accordance with HIPAA requirements and organizational policies  
- Tracking referrals, follow-up activity, scheduling status, and outcomes to ensure that no inquiry is overlooked  
- Remaining organized, responsive, and professional while managing multiple calls, referrals, and admissions tasks  
- Monitoring patient safety, behavior, vital signs, and overall condition in a psychiatric hospital setting  
- Supporting patients with personal care, daily activities, socialization, and rehabilitation  
- Remaining calm and effective during high-stress conversations and crisis situations  

I am passionate about helping adolescents and families connect with the appropriate behavioral health and substance use treatment services. My combination of hands-on psychiatric experience, referral coordination, insurance verification, admissions support, documentation, and strong interpersonal skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your virtual admissions team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of your organization. I look forward to hearing from you.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over five years of experience in behavioral health and substance use recovery, including client admissions, intake coordination, documentation, and compassionate client support, I bring a strong foundation in helping individuals navigate treatment and access the care they need.

In my current role as a Recovery Specialist at High Point Treatment Center, I complete client admissions and intakes, maintain accurate documentation, support compliance with program requirements, and help facilitate smooth transitions into treatment. Working in a structured behavioral health setting serving individuals with mental health and substance use disorders has strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, recognize client needs, maintain confidentiality, and prioritize safety. Being recognized as Employee of the Year in March 2024 reflects my commitment to professionalism, reliability, and the quality of care I provide.

I understand that the admissions process is often the first meaningful connection a client or family has with a treatment program. I would approach every inquiry with patience, compassion, and clear communication while helping callers understand their options and navigate the next steps toward care. My experience with intake procedures, data entry, documentation, and CRM software has prepared me to manage information accurately, maintain organized workflows, and follow through on important details. I am also comfortable working within established procedures and handling sensitive information with the discretion and confidentiality required in behavioral health.

In addition to my clinical support experience, my previous management roles strengthened my organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills. I managed competing priorities, maintained accurate records, coached team members, and ensured consistent follow-through in fast-paced environments. These experiences have prepared me to manage an admissions pipeline, coordinate multiple responsibilities, and remain accountable in a remote position.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines my behavioral health experience with my passion for helping people take meaningful steps toward recovery. I would welcome the opportunity to support both adolescent mental health services and adult substance use treatment by helping prospective clients and their families feel heard, informed, and supported from their first contact through the admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, admissions and intake skills, and commitment to compassionate client care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,
Alison Vasques

Kris Secor
Barberville, FL
(386) 453-1015

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

Howdy! I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy because this role reflects the kind of work I have spent years doing: showing up for people when they are struggling, building trust when trust does not come easily, and helping individuals feel supported without judgment.
I bring more than seven years of direct behavioral health experience working with children, adolescents, adults, and older adults facing complex mental health, behavioral, and co-occurring substance use challenges. At Promises Behavioral Health, I supported adults ages 18 to 81 in residential and partial hospitalization settings. My work required constant observation, strong boundaries, de-escalation, crisis response, accurate documentation working with Kipu, teamwork with clinicians, and—perhaps most importantly—the ability to connect with people who were overwhelmed, guarded, resistant, or simply having a very difficult day.
Before that, at Halifax Behavioral Health, I worked with at-risk children and adolescents ages 4 to 17. That experience taught me how much can be communicated without words and how important consistency, patience, calmness, and genuine human connection are when someone does not yet feel safe enough to engage.
Those same lessons have followed me throughout nearly three decades of equine work. Through my current business, Healed By The Horse, I create individualized experiences centered on trust, emotional awareness, regulation, confidence, and connection. Horses have reinforced something I already knew from behavioral health: you cannot force trust. You earn it by being present, observant, consistent, and authentic.
That is what draws me to remote work with Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I understand that meaningful mental health is not achieved by treating a diagnosis while overlooking the person living with it. People need to know that someone sees them, hears them, respects their experience, and will continue showing up. I would bring that mindset—along with substantial hands-on behavioral health experience, strong observational skills, compassion, professional boundaries, and a steady presence—to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role.
I am also comfortable working independently, communicating virtually, documenting electronically via Kipu, learning new systems, and collaborating closely with multidisciplinary care teams. The opportunity to provide meaningful support within a virtual treatment environment is especially appealing to me.
I would be proud to bring my experience, patience, intuition, and very genuine commitment to helping people to Adolescent Wellness Academy. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how I could contribute to your team and, most importantly, to the individuals you serve.

Warmly,

Kris Secor

candidates.cover_letter:
Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in psychology, behavioral health, crisis support, and working directly with children and families, I was immediately drawn to this opportunity because of the importance you place on making the first point of contact compassionate, supportive, and clear.

Throughout my experience in behavioral health, I have learned that the way someone is treated during their first interaction can significantly affect whether they feel comfortable accepting help. In my work as a Behavioral Therapist/RBT, I have provided individualized behavioral support to children, communicated closely with parents and caregivers, maintained confidential documentation, assisted with scheduling and insurance coordination, and supported families through challenging behavioral situations. This experience has required patience, organization, professionalism, and the ability to communicate complicated information in a way that families can easily understand.

My crisis-support experience has strengthened these skills even further. As a Youth Crisis Counselor and Suicide Prevention Crisis Line Volunteer, I supported individuals during highly emotional and vulnerable moments through active listening, crisis intervention, risk and safety assessment, de-escalation, and connection to appropriate resources. These experiences taught me how to remain calm when someone on the other end of the conversation may be scared, overwhelmed, frustrated, or unsure of what to do next.

I also understand that effective admissions coordination requires more than compassion. It requires strong follow-through. My professional experience includes scheduling, insurance coordination, detailed documentation, maintaining confidentiality, communicating with families, and independently managing responsibilities. I am comfortable working with technology and learning new systems, and I understand the importance of accurate, timely, and HIPAA-compliant documentation when working in behavioral health.

I am especially interested in this position because it combines the administrative side of behavioral healthcare with direct human connection. I would value the opportunity to help a parent searching for treatment for their teenager, an individual seeking help for substance use or mental health concerns, or a provider trying to connect someone with an appropriate level of care. Even when a program is not the right fit, I believe every person deserves to leave that interaction feeling heard, respected, and clearer about what they can do next.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience, crisis-support background, communication skills, and commitment to compassionate care to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Brianna Otero
